title: Winter Term Academic Calendar 2025-26
content:
The winter term of 2025-26 opens on 5 January 2026 with orientation in North Campus. Mid-term assessments run 16 to 21 February, the spring recess is 23 to 28 March, and the last teaching day is 24 April 2026. Grade release for the winter term is scheduled for 15 May. Calendar queries go to calendar.office@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: End-Semester Examination Hall Rules
content:
Candidates must reach the examination hall 20 minutes before the start and carry the printed hall ticket with a photograph. Smart watches, fitness bands and earbuds are banned inside the hall. No candidate may leave during the first 45 minutes or the last 10 minutes. Spare answer booklets are issued only after the main booklet is fully used. Report clashes to exam.cell@thornwick.example or helpline (0181) 419 7627.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Central Library Extended Hours During Examinations
content:
From 1 December to 20 December the Central Library in Willowbank Annex stays open 7:00 AM to 1:00 AM on all days, including Sundays. The silent reading floor (Level 3) is reserved for exam preparation, and group study pods must be booked through the library kiosk for at most 2 hours per day. Night shuttle drop-off to the hostels runs at 11:30 PM and 1:10 AM. Contact library.desk@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Hostel Visitor and Mess Timing Rules
content:
Day visitors may meet residents only in the hostel lounge between 4:00 PM and 7:30 PM, and must sign the visitor register with photo ID. Overnight guests are not allowed. The mess serves breakfast 7:15-9:00, lunch 12:30-2:00 and dinner 7:30-9:30; residents who skip more than 8 consecutive meals may apply for a mess rebate. Kettles and induction cookers are confiscated on inspection. Warden office: hostel.warden@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Online Fee Payment Procedure Through the Student Portal
content:
Semester fees are paid online through the Thornwick student portal under Finance > Pay Dues. Supported modes are net banking, UPI and debit card; credit card payments carry a 1.2 percent convenience charge. After payment the portal generates an e-receipt with a 14-character transaction reference, which must be kept for the hall ticket check. Payment failures are reversed by the bank within 7 working days. Finance help desk: fees.help@thornwick.example, (0181) 545 9261.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Undergraduate Admissions Frequently Asked Questions
content:
Applicants can submit one online form for up to three programmes. The application fee is 1,200 rupees and is not refundable. Merit lists are published in three rounds, and seat acceptance requires a deposit of 25,000 rupees within 5 days of the offer. Lateral entry to the second year is open only to diploma holders with 60 percent marks. Admission office: admissions@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Thornwick Merit-cum-Means Bursary Announcement
content:
The Thornwick Merit-cum-Means Bursary for 2026 offers 40 awards of 30,000 rupees each to first-year students whose family income is below 6 lakh rupees per year. Applications open 10 August and close 31 August, and need an income certificate and the class 12 mark sheet. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed online in the second week of September. Write to bursary.office@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Photography Club Recruitment Notice
content:
The Shutterbugs Photography Club is recruiting first- and second-year members. Applicants submit a portfolio of 5 photographs on the theme 'Campus After Rain' by 12 September. The club runs a darkroom workshop every Friday in Cedar Court and a heritage photo walk each month. Membership is free; the club lends two DSLR kits on a weekly rota. Club e-mail: photoclub@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Campus Map and Building Directory
content:
The main gate opens onto the central avenue. Administrative offices are in Heron Wing; engineering departments occupy Kestrel Block and Falcon Block; the medical centre sits behind Victoria Lawn; and the sports complex is on Riverside Campus across the footbridge. Lecture theatres are numbered LT-1 to LT-9 starting from the north end. Ramps and lifts are available in every block except the old Heron Wing, where the ground floor is step-free.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: IT Help Desk Guide to Campus Wi-Fi Setup
content:
The campus wireless network is called TW-Secure and uses WPA2-Enterprise. Students sign in with their portal username and a separate Wi-Fi password created at wifi.thornwick.example. Each user may register at most 3 devices; gaming consoles must be registered through the help desk with their MAC address. Forgotten Wi-Fi passwords can be reset at the self-service kiosk in the library foyer. Help desk: it.helpdesk@thornwick.example, (0181) 788 1215.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Campus Shuttle Bus Timetable
content:
Shuttle route S1 loops Main Gate - Kestrel Block - Larch Hall - Riverside Campus every 15 minutes from 7:30 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays. Route S2 connects the hostels to the city bus terminus at 8:10 AM, 1:40 PM and 6:20 PM. Weekend service runs every 40 minutes. The bus pass costs 900 rupees per semester and is loaded onto the student ID card. Transport office: transport@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Inter-Department Football Tournament 2025
content:
The inter-department football tournament runs from 3 to 14 November 2025 on the Riverside Campus turf. Each department may register one squad of 16 players by 27 October. Matches are 2 x 30 minutes with rolling substitutions. The winning team receives the Founders' Shield and each player gets a 1,500-rupee sports store voucher. Contact sports.office@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Placement Cell Registration Notice for Final-Year Students
content:
Final-year students who wish to sit for campus recruitment must register on the placement portal by 20 July and upload a one-page resume in PDF. Students who accept one offer are not eligible for further drives, except for offers that pay at least 1.5 times the first one. Mock interviews start on 1 August in Victoria Lawn. Placement office: placements@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Anti-Ragging Undertaking and Helpline
content:
Every newly admitted student and one parent must sign the online anti-ragging undertaking before the first day of classes; hostel keys are not issued without it. The anti-ragging squad makes surprise night rounds in the first 8 weeks. Victims or witnesses can call the 24-hour helpline (0181) 393 1107 or write to antiragging@thornwick.example, and may remain anonymous. Proven ragging can lead to rustication and withdrawal of the degree.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Online Grievance Portal and Appeal Timelines
content:
A student grievance is first lodged online on the grievance portal and is acknowledged within 2 working days. The departmental grievance cell must resolve it within 15 working days; if the student is not satisfied, an appeal goes to the University Grievance Committee within 10 days of the decision. Grievances about grades are handled separately under the re-evaluation rules. Ombudsperson office: grievance@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Answer Script Re-evaluation Rules
content:
Students may apply for re-evaluation of an end-semester answer script within 7 days of result declaration. The fee is 750 rupees per paper and is refunded if the mark rises by 10 percent or more. A photocopy of the evaluated script can be requested for 300 rupees. Re-evaluated marks are final, whether higher or lower. Applications: reval@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Medical Centre Services and Hours
content:
The campus medical centre behind Victoria Lawn is open 24 hours with a resident doctor from 8 AM to 10 PM and a nurse on night duty. A general physician, dentist (Tuesday and Friday) and counsellor (weekdays) are available. Ambulance requests: (0181) 733 9224. Medical certificates for missed assessments must be issued by the centre or verified by it within 3 days.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Student Counselling and Wellbeing Service
content:
Free and confidential counselling is available to all students in Cedar Court, Room W-12. Sessions are 45 minutes and can be booked online or by walking in between 10 AM and 5 PM. The service also runs a weekly 'exam stress' group and peer-listener training each semester. Nothing discussed is shared with departments without consent, except where there is a risk to life. E-mail: wellbeing@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Bicycle Sharing Scheme on Campus
content:
The green-cycle scheme has 120 bicycles at 8 docking points across North Campus and Riverside Campus. Rides of up to 30 minutes are free; each extra 30 minutes costs 10 rupees. Bicycles must be returned to a dock by 10 PM. Damage must be reported in the app within one hour of the ride. Scheme desk: greencycle@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Lost and Found Procedure
content:
Items found on campus should be handed to the security office at the main gate, where they are logged with date and place found. Unclaimed items are kept for 60 days; ID cards are sent to the registrar after 7 days. Owners claim items by describing them and showing a student or staff ID. Electronic devices are wiped before donation. Security office: (0181) 788 6965.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Language Lab Booking Rules
content:
The language lab in Victoria Lawn has 36 headset stations with pronunciation software for English, French, German and Japanese. Students may book a station for up to 90 minutes per day through the lab calendar. Food and drink are not allowed, and headsets must be wiped after use. The lab assistant can be reached at langlab@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Student ID Card Replacement Process
content:
A lost or damaged student ID card is replaced after the student files a loss declaration on the portal and pays 400 rupees. The replacement is ready in 3 working days at the card office in North Campus. The old card is blocked immediately, including its library and shuttle functions. Bring one passport-size photograph. Card office: idcard@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Blood Donation Camp Notice
content:
The National Service Scheme unit will hold a blood donation camp on 8 October 2025 from 9 AM to 4 PM in Phoenix Lab. Donors must be 18 to 60 years old, weigh at least 50 kg and not have donated in the last 3 months. Every donor receives a certificate and refreshments. Register at nss.unit@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Annual Cultural Festival Volunteer Call
content:
Lumina, the annual cultural festival, takes place 6 to 8 February 2026. The organising committee needs 150 student volunteers for hospitality, stage management, security and the food court. Volunteers get a certificate, a festival T-shirt and free entry to the closing concert. Sign-up closes 15 January. Contact lumina.fest@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Swimming Pool Access Rules
content:
The 25-metre pool on Riverside Campus is open 6:00-8:30 AM and 5:00-8:00 PM. Students need a medical fitness certificate and a swimming cap; non-swimmers may use only lanes 1 and 2 under a lifeguard. Women-only sessions run on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. The pool closes during thunderstorms. Sports office: (0181) 733 8161.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Printing and Photocopy Quota for Students
content:
Each student receives a free printing quota of 200 pages per semester, loaded onto the ID card. Extra pages cost 1 rupee for black and white and 8 rupees for colour. Unused quota does not carry over. Print release stations are in the library, Kestrel Block and Larch Hall. Report printer faults to it.helpdesk@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Convocation 2026 Registration
content:
The 2026 convocation will be held on 21 March 2026 in the open-air theatre at Victoria Lawn. Graduating students must register by 20 February and collect gowns from 18 to 20 March against a refundable deposit of 1,000 rupees. Each graduate may bring two guests. Graduates who cannot attend can receive the degree by post. Contact convocation@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Canteen Food Safety and Pricing Notice
content:
All campus canteens display a fixed price list approved by the canteen committee; a standard thali costs 70 rupees and tea 10 rupees. Food safety inspections are held every month and the latest hygiene score is posted at each counter. Complaints about quality or overcharging can be dropped in the box at Heron Wing or sent to canteen.committee@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Disability Support and Accessibility Services
content:
Students with a disability can register with the accessibility office to receive exam accommodations such as extra time (20 minutes per hour), a scribe, a ground-floor room or screen-reader software. Requests must reach the office 21 days before the examination. Accessible rooms are available in every hostel. Contact accessibility@thornwick.example or (0181) 771 5215.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Environmental Club Tree Plantation Drive
content:
The Green Roots environmental club will plant 500 native saplings along the north boundary of North Campus on 5 June 2026, World Environment Day. Volunteers meet at Willowbank Annex at 7 AM; gloves and tools are provided. Each volunteer adopts one sapling and records its growth for a year. Register at greenroots@thornwick.example.

This notice is issued by the Office of the Registrar, Thornwick University.

title: Grading Policy and Relative Grading Bands
content:
From the 2025-26 session, courses with more than 40 students use relative grading. The O grade is limited to the top 7 percent, A+ to the next 13 percent and A to the next 20 percent. A course coordinator who wants to depart from the bands must file a justification with the Dean. Absolute grading continues for labs and courses with fewer than 40 students. Queries: Dr. Arjit Dhingra (arjit.dhingra@thornwick.example, +91 98561 37471).

Minutes recorded by Mr. Raghav Achrekar; follow-up actions tracked by Prof. Tanvi Chitnis (tanvi.chitnis@thornwick.example, (0181) 524 5758).

title: Moderation of End-Semester Answer Scripts
content:
Each end-semester course is moderated by a second examiner who re-marks a random 10 percent sample of scripts. If the average difference exceeds 8 percent, the whole batch is re-marked by a third examiner. Moderation reports must be filed within 5 days of marking. The moderation coordinator for this session is Prof. Raghav Limaye (raghav.limaye@thornwick.example, 98498-25887).

Minutes recorded by Dr. Ojas Bhatia; follow-up actions tracked by Ms. Ira Khurana (ira.khurana@thornwick.example, (0181) 736 4789).

title: Odd Semester Timetable and Room Allocation
content:
The odd semester timetable uses 50-minute slots from 8:30 AM, with Wednesday afternoon kept free for clubs. Large lecture theatres LT-1 to LT-3 are reserved for first-year common courses. Departments must submit room change requests by 25 July; after that only swaps between departments are allowed. Room allocation is managed by Prof. Mrinal Rege in Kestrel Block.

content:

Chief superintendent for Kestrel Block is Ms. Akshara Raval (akshara.raval@thornwick.example, (0181) 510 7158); for Larch Hall it is Dr. Mahika Sawhney (mahika.sawhney@thornwick.example, +91 98793 87949). content:
The Research Office invites proposals for internal seed grants of up to 3 lakh rupees for 12 months. Priority areas are water treatment, low-cost sensors and assistive technology. Only faculty who joined after January 2023 may apply as principal investigator. The proposal deadline is 15 February 2026. content:

content:

content:

Faculty reviewers are needed; each reviewer handles 4 papers. Conference secretary: Mr. Rohit Tandon (rohit.tandon@thornwick.example, +91 98135 45787).

Minutes recorded by Ms. Aruna Kohli; follow-up actions tracked by Mr. Sonal Mehrotra (sonal.mehrotra@thornwick.example, (0181) 606 3516).

title: Internal Marks Submission Deadline - Odd Semester
content:
Internal assessment marks for the odd semester must be uploaded to the academic portal by 5:00 PM on 12 November 2025. Marks cannot be edited after the portal locks; changes need the Dean's approval with a written reason. Students with less than 40 percent internal marks must be flagged for a make-up test. Portal help: Mr. Kabir Bhandari (kabir.bhandari@thornwick.example, (0181) 698 1045).

Minutes recorded by Mr. Payal Rajput; follow-up actions tracked by Dr. Kritika Sethi (kritika.sethi@thornwick.example, +91 98788 37432).

title: Chemistry Laboratory Safety Rules
content:
All users of the chemistry labs in Phoenix Lab must wear a lab coat, goggles and closed shoes. Fume hoods must be used for volatile solvents, and acid waste goes only into the labelled yellow carboys. Eye-wash stations are tested every Monday. Any spill above 100 ml must be reported to the lab safety officer Dr. Dhruv Salvi (dhruv.salvi@thornwick.example, +91 98624 52029) within one hour.

title: Faculty Leave Rules - Casual and Earned Leave
content:
Faculty are entitled to 8 days of casual leave and 15 days of earned leave per year. Casual leave cannot be combined with vacation, and more than 3 consecutive days need a substitute arrangement for classes. Earned leave can be carried forward up to 180 days. Leave applications go through the HR portal; the leave section officer is Prof. Akshara Tilak (akshara.tilak@thornwick.example, 98282-49700).
